Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

somehow adverb

also somehow or other, in some way, one way or another, by any means, some way or other

classical

Cic. de Or. 2.232: quis haec nōn vel facile vel certē aliquō modō posset ēdiscere? (Lewis & Short)
Plaut. Stich. 4.2.41: exōrābō aliquō modō (Lewis & Short)

aliquō modō

phrase: ablative of manner

somehow, in some way

The plain phrase: by some means, not said which.

Other words

  • nesciō quō modō (nesciō quōmodo) — somehow, I don’t know how

    phrase used as a parenthesis, without changing the mood of the verb · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.146: fit enim, nesciō quōmodo, ut (Lewis & Short); Cic. Sest. 100: bonī nesciō quōmodo tardiōrēs sunt (Lewis & Short)

    Said in passing, as English says “somehow”, of what happens one cannot tell how (Lewis & Short, s.v. nesciō).

  • quōquō modō — somehow or other, by any means, however you can

    phrase · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.4.3: quōquō modō potes ad mē fac veniās; Cic. Q. fr. 1.2.4: tū quōquō modō hominem investīgēs velim (Lewis & Short)

    Of getting something done whatever it takes.

  • aliquā — somehow, one way or another

    adverb · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 5.1.19 (Lewis & Short); Plaut. Merc. 2.2.62 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    Its first sense is “somewhere, by some way”; in comedy, “in some way or other” (Lewis & Short).

  • quōmodocumque — in whatever way, however

    also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 5.30: quōmodocumque dīcitur, intellegī tamen potest (Lewis & Short); Traupman 162: some way or other

    Classically “in whatever way”, a relative adverb; for “somehow or other” aliquō modō is the classical phrase.

Examples

  • tū mihi aliquid aliquō modō alicunde ab aliquibus blatīs

    you babble something to me, somehow, from somewhere, from someonePlaut. Epid. 3.1.13 (Lewis & Short)

  • bonī nesciō quōmodo tardiōrēs sunt

    good men are somehow slowerCic. Sest. 100 (Lewis & Short)

  • sī est spēs nostrī reditūs, eam cōnfīrmēs et rem adjuvēs; sīn, ut ego metuō, trānsāctum est, quōquō modō potes ad mē fac veniās.

    if there is hope of my return, strengthen it and help the cause; but if, as I fear, it is all over, come to me somehow, however you can.Cic. Fam. 14.4.3

See also how, manner, somewhere, someone.
